svg.text: Vehicle breaching — the contact cue, the gaps, the bulldozer's point order (DESIGN_Vehicle_Breaching.md §7, §7.6; house style)
Scope: the NEW contact cue, the gaps as drawn, the ClearObstacle At field and its verdict. The HUD, the Orders tab and the maps are context (UNCHANGED). Grey notes are not drawn by the app.
A1 — driving a possessed IFV into a sandbag wall, throttle held: the PUSH (D-3)

NEW: dust where the hull meets it (V-17)
Context, unchanged: the compass strip, the crosshair, the bottom-left block (HEALTH green, the selected weapon yellow,
the others grey-white, the seat line, the keys grey). A RAM (speed into the wall ≥ the row's minimum) breaks at once —
no bar; a PUSH fills it, and it empties if the throttle is released or the hull leaves contact. A break costs speed,
never stops the hull dead (V-3).
A2 — a possessed HMMWV at a building wall: held
Red, held while in contact: a wheeled vehicle never breaks (B-D3);
an IFV at a building wall says the same. Also at a low wall (D-4).
A3 — a possessed tank's bump on a building wall: the break

g.text: BREACHED — a way in for infantry

svg.text: Green for ~2 s, then gone. Dust + a crash sound (AI hears it, V-17).
The tank stays OUT of the gap it made (B-D4, V-5).

route once the navmesh has the gap (the bake); sight and fire pass at once (query time,
B-D8). The tank's own hull purpose ignores a building-wall breach (V-5).

Both draw the gap from the damage RECORD (V-16 — today the re-cut lives in the bake, which only
a navmesh node runs): the editor, the player, display nodes and the Replay Browser alike. The
rubble line is the mesh's; vehicles and infantry route through it (acceptance 6, 14).

ParamsDto drawn by the ONE field drawer — the entity chip + teal pick glyph (EntityLink); x y z +
Pick Map + List… (a point; List… only where named points exist); defaults grey at 0. NEW: the At
row and under it the resolver's VERDICT (green: a wall cut / an obstacle; amber: nothing within
3 m — the order would fail). Obstacle set ⇒ today's path, unchanged (the company's roadblock
call). The 3 m pick radius and a 60 s timeout are open tunables (§7.6). Task group: Library/Engineer.

The ring = the resolver's 3 m: an obstacle in it wins (today's push, the
entity's Health); else the wall panels in it ⇒ a blade-wide, full-height
Passage at the point (V-6, V-13). The verdict shows at the pick and in
the form; the brain drives, the Muscle cuts (one breach writer).
